messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?
I've just started mining. So all I have is a nerd QX plus plus rev six point one. And I'm potentially looking to add another one. So that's what brought me to to your site.
Oh nice — so you're already running a NerdQaxe++ Rev 6.1. Let me pull that up actually — Tell me about the first one — when did you get it, and what made you pick that specific unit to start with?
Uh, I got it about one month ago, and I picked it based on price and the six terahash speed.
Got it — about a month in. And you're already thinking about a second one, so something's clicking. What is it about the experience so far that's making you want to add another?
Uh, well, a friend of mine bought one at the same time, and he already hit a Bitcoin block. So, uh, wanna keep going and potentially add another one.

Wait — your friend hit a block on a single NerdQaxe in the first month?? That's wild. Lottery odds.

So is that the draw for you too — the lottery hit? Or is it something else about
Yes. Yes. Yeah. The water hit. No. The lottery hit. Yeah. Solo mining lottery hit.

Yeah okay — solo lottery. So your friend basically just hit the jackpot a month in and now you're thinking "if I double my tickets, I double my odds."

Did you and your friend buy together originally, or did you find HD on your own?
IPhone HD on my own bought our original ones just off a local uh, Facebook marketplace ad.
Oh interesting — so the first NerdQaxe came off Facebook Marketplace, not HD. Was that a used unit from someone local in Edmonton?
Yep. No. It was brand new that someone in Edmonton brought in whole bunch of them and then sold them off individually.

Ah — so somebody in Edmonton imported a batch and flipped them individually on Marketplace. Smart little side hustle.

So now for unit two, you're looking at HD directly instead of going back to that Marketplace seller. Why the switch?

Uh, the HD unit comes with a much better power supply. And, uh, with the baffle on the heat sink to cool the the power units. And also coming from HD, it'll come with some warranty where the marketplace one comes with no warranty.

Okay that's really specific — better PSU, the baffle on the heatsink, and the warranty. So you've clearly looked closely at both.

Did you have a problem with the Marketplace unit's PSU or cooling? Or did you just notice the spec difference when you were browsing HD?
No. I I had an issue with the, uh, with the PSU well, actually, the board heatsink, uh, overheating. And shutting down. Uh, so this is why I'm looking at a better unit with a better power supply.

Ah — so the Marketplace one is actually thermal-throttling and shutting down on you. That's frustrating after a month.

Where do you have it running right now — what room?
It's spreading, uh, upstairs in my office. Right now, the temperatures in Edmonton, uh, have have been sitting at twenty degrees Celsius or lower.

Okay — so it's in your office upstairs, and even with Edmonton at 20°C or below ambient, it's still overheating. That tells you something about that unit specifically.

When summer hits and the office warms up, what's your plan? Same room, or are you going to move it somewhere cooler?
I'm gonna probably move them to the basement where it's probably gonna be sixteen degrees Celsius.

Smart — basement at 16°C will be way kinder to them.

So the office right now — is the NerdQaxe sitting out on your desk where you can see it, or is it tucked away somewhere out of sight?
It's where I can see it.
Nice. The O. display and the look of that unit — does that matter to you, having it visible? Or is it more that the office is just where the ethernet and power happened to be?
It's right now where the Ethernet is, uh, except this unit runs on Wi Fi, so it can be anywheres. And, yeah, I'd like to see it.
Yeah — "I'd like to see it." Say more about that. What do you get out of being able to see it sitting there?
While you're always looking for that block found message popping up on it.

Ha — yeah, checking for the block-found message. So it's almost like a slot machine you walk past every day.

Does anyone else in the house notice it? Like does your family ask about it, or is this purely your thing?
Uh, when I'm away, they pop in and take a look at it to see if it says anything. And that's where they saw the thermal overheat. Message pop up.

Oh that's great — so your family is checking on it for you when you're away. They're invested too.

And they're the ones who flagged the overheating message — that's actually a really useful early-warning system. Did that change how you think about where to put unit two, or are they kind of part of the fun now?
Unit two, I probably have more confidence putting it, uh, just with the better quality unit, keeping it in my office and putting the old one in the basement.

Oh that's a clever split — trust the new HD one upstairs where you can watch it, banish the flaky one to the basement. Makes total sense.

Let me ask about the page you're looking at — this Mining Rewards Estimate section — have you looked at this
I'm looking at yes.
What do you make of it? Does it match what you've been seeing on your unit so far, or are you using something else to estimate?
Yeah. I've been looking at different sites on the Internet to estimate. But, um, right now, my plan is to not mine bitcoin, but mine bitcoin cash. And or maybe Litecoin with it. Haven't decided yet.

Wait — hold on. Bitcoin Cash or Litecoin on a NerdQaxe? That's an SHA-256 / ASIC unit — Litecoin is Scrypt, totally different algorithm. You can't mine Litecoin on it.

Where did you hear you could? I want to make sure I understand what you're planning.

Okay. Okay. No. Then this one probably wouldn't be Litecoin. Maybe it's some other coin, uh, that a friend of mine is thinking about mining with his and and setting up a solo node for it. But right now, I have it mining Bitcoin cash.

Ah okay — Bitcoin Cash makes sense, same SHA-256 so the NerdQaxe works fine there. Got it.

So why Bitcoin Cash instead of Bitcoin? Is it the lower difficulty making a solo hit more realistic, or something else about BCH you like?
Uh, no. The better odds for a solo hit.

Yeah that makes sense — way fewer competitors on BCH solo, so the lottery math is more in your favor.

Has your friend who hit the block — was that on Bitcoin or Bitcoin Cash?
On Bitcoin Cash.
Aha — so the success story you're chasing is actually a BCH block, not BTC. That changes things. Was it a meaningful payout dollar-wise, or more like a "holy crap it actually happened" moment?
I think it was, uh, yeah. Holy crap. It actually happened, uh, within a week of getting the unit.

Within a week — wow. Okay so that's a powerful anchor in your head right now. Hit happens fast, double the units, double the tickets.

Let me show you something — this comparison table on the homepage — did you happen to scroll down to this when you were browsing last night?
Let me look.
Take your time — I can see you had a session last night around 11:21 PM where you bounced between the NerdQaxe and the NerdOctaxe. Curious if this table was part of how you were thinking about it.
Oh, yeah. I was looking at, uh, just a comparison. In price and and speed. And deciding which one I wanted for my second one.

Got it — so you used the table to weigh NerdQaxe vs NerdOctaxe. Walk me through that — what made you keep landing back on the NerdQaxe at $249 instead of jumping to the NerdOctaxe at $499 for double the hashrate?
Well, I haven't hundred percent decided yet. So
Fair — you're still deciding. What's the

again, Yeah. Prices are good. Yeah. Prices are good. Your sale on the on the, uh, on the NerdQX plus plus, it is what really drew me to your page. Also, what drew me to your page I follow Red Panda. And, uh, he just recently put out a YouTube video which linked your page.

Yeah, Red Panda sends a lot of folks our way — makes sense.

So back to NerdQaxe vs NerdOctaxe — the Octaxe is double the hashrate for double the price, basically same $/TH. If the whole game is more lottery tickets, the Octaxe gives you more tickets per dollar of shelf space and power. What's pulling you back toward a second NerdQaxe instead?
Okay.
What's going through your head right now on that — Octaxe vs a second NerdQaxe?
Oh, it's just how much do I wanna spend right now? Uh, because like I say, both look good to me.

Yeah — so it's really just a budget ceiling thing right now, not a spec preference. Totally fair.

When you think about that ceiling — is there a number in your head, like "I'd spend $X on this hobby this month but not $Y"? Or is it more vibes-based?
It's it's four dollars and pop cost of power and yeah, in odds
Sorry — you cut out a little there. Did you say it's about the cost of power plus the odds? Walk me through how you're thinking about that.
Yeah. Just it's the total cost of of running one. So the cost excuse me, the cost of purchasing one, cost of running one, how many terahash do I need?

Got it — so it's a whole-system calculation, not just the sticker. Purchase + power + how much hashrate you actually need to make the lottery feel worth it.

On the power side — do you know what your electricity rate is in Edmonton, and have you actually run the math on what one NerdQaxe costs you per month to run?
Right now, our power rate is low. It's five point eight cents per kilowatt hour. So right now, it's cheap to run them.
Oh wow
But I haven't run the yeah. I haven't run the total number

5.8 cents is amazing — that's like a third of what a lot of US folks pay. So power's basically a non-issue for you right now. That actually shifts the math toward "more hashrate is better" since you're not getting punished for watts.

Has the cheap power influenced you at all toward looking at bigger units — like did you ever consider something way bigger, or is the NerdQaxe class just where your comfort zone is?
No. I I'm considering a bigger one. As well. I'm considering the Antminer, uh, twenty one XP.
Oh — okay, now we're talking. The A. S21 XP is a totally different tier — like 270 TH/s, way more serious money, way more noise. What's pulling you toward that?

Um, the just the hash rate of of of having two hundred and seventy terahash in one unit working on one block, and having that much better odds uh, what's pulling me away from it is the noise of having it in the house.

There it is — noise. So the S21 XP is basically a jet engine, 75 dB+, and you've already said you want to *see* your miner in your office. Those two things don't coexist.

Have you thought about where an S21 XP would even live? Garage? Shed? Or is the noise the thing that keeps pulling you back to NerdQaxe class?
It would live in the basement, and I would have to replace the fans with uh, a silent or silent fan unit.
Ah okay — so you've already been researching fan swaps. That's a pretty deep rabbit hole. Where'd you pick that up — Red Panda, Reddit, somewhere else?
Uh, read it online. Yeah. A little bit of Gemini.
Gemini — like asking the AI directly? That's interesting. So you're using Gemini as a research tool for this whole hobby?
Yeah. Yes.

That's really useful for me to know. What kind of stuff have you been asking it — like spec comparisons, troubleshooting your overheating unit, fan mods? Walk me through a recent question you put to it.

I put to it, um, wiring size, power consumption, which plug I should be installing, uh, whether I should use a PDU or direct cable. Things like that. And it gave me pros and cons on all those questions.

Okay so you're going pretty deep — electrical infrastructure, PDU vs direct, wire gauge. That's not casual hobby stuff, that's "I'm planning a real setup" stuff.

Is there a vision in your head of where this goes? Like a year from now, what does your setup look like — still two NerdQaxes in the office, or something bigger?
Probably two nerd axes or nerd ax class type of machines in the office. Antminer twenty one XP in the basement, and maybe one more space heater type machine running at my son's place.

Oh that's a really clear vision actually — distributed across two locations, mix of "watch and enjoy" units in the office, a workhorse in the basement, and one at your son's place as a space heater that happens to mine.

Tell me about your son's place — is he into this too, or is this more you setting him up?
It's me setting him up. He has free power. But uh, only a hundred and twenty volts.

Ha — free power but 120V only, so you're cap····what you can put there. That's basically a NerdQaxe or Bitaxe class unit territory, not an S21.

Free power at his place is wild though — is that a roommate situation, utilities-included rental, something like that?
Yes. The utility included rental.

Got it. So the hobby is also kind of a family thing — your son's place, your family checking the OLED when you're away. That's cool.

Let me ask you one more thing — this banner on the product image — "Free return shipping & RMA" — do you know what RMA means?
Yeah. RMA is what you get if you need to return something.

Perfect — yeah, return merchandise authorization. A lot of folks don't know that acronym, good to confirm.

Speaking of returns — given your Marketplace unit is overheating and you're now coming to HD partly for the warranty, how much did warranty/RMA actually weigh in your decision to come here vs another vendor? Did you look at other sites too?

Yes. We have some local sites. Um, even with the dollar exchange rate, your price is right in line with them. But, um, what brought me here was just the Red Panda recommendation and the power supply that you're including versus the simple brick power supply.

Got it — so it's Red Panda's rec plus the upgraded PSU that won out, even with USD-CAD exchange in play. Warranty was a nice-to-have, not the deciding factor.

What are the local Canadian sites you compared against? I want to make sure I know who you were weighing us against.
Give me a second.
Take your
Miner Mart. Yeah. Miner Mart Canada.
Miner Mart Canada — got it, that's super useful. Anyone else, or was Miner Mart the main comparison?
Uh, they were the main one. Then there's I think it's DS Central.

DS Central and Miner Mart Canada — perfect, noted.

Last question and then I'll let you go — you've been incredibly helpful. Is there anything I didn't ask about that you wish I had? Anything that's been on your mind about HD, the buying process, or this hobby in general?
No. The only other comment is uh, you guys ship from a Canadian warehouse. So that makes dealing with cross border and, uh, border a nonissue.

Oh that's huge — yeah, Canadian warehouse means no customs surprise, no brokerage fees, no waiting at the border. Glad that landed for you.

Dave, this has been genuinely one of the more useful conversations I've had this week — the Marketplace overheating story, the BCH solo strategy, the three-location vision with your son's place, Miner Mart and DS Central as comparisons, and Gemini as your research tool — all really valuable. Your $75 discount code will hit your email shortly.

Good luck with unit two, and tell your friend congrats on that BCH block from me. Have a great day!
Great. Thank you.
Take care, Dave!
Bye bye.
Bye for now.
